In this regime, a simple mean over the full 19-model pool provides the most robust aggregation: it avoids overfitting to 3 noisy validation windows, does not chase per-window winners, and benefits from the diversity of 19 models despite their correlated errors. All my trimmed-mean and pruned-pool variants scored worse, confirming that removing models or trimming tails only discards useful signal without reducing correlated-error drag.
